full_judgment:
3. Plaintiffs' case, in short, was that the nature of the suit land was homestead and pond and it belonged to Maharaja Sitangshu Kumar Acharjee Chowdhury. The predecessor of the plaintiffs, Abdul Hye Sujan took rokka pattan of the suit land on 18th Kartic 1351 BS and since then he had been in possession therein by constructing dwelling house, excavating pond and rearing fish. Preliminary record of right was prepared in the name of Abdul Hye Sujan, but finally was prepared in the name of the Government. Said Abdul Hye Sujan died on 30-9-1996 leaving behind the plaintiffs as his legal heirs. Thus the predecessor of the plaintiffs and after his death the plaintiffs had/have been possessing the suit land for more than 60 years. The plaintiffs came to know about the wrong recording of the record of right in the name of the Government for the first time on 2-5-2002 which created, cloud over their title to the suit land, hence the suit. 

 6. Mr Zainul Abedin, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, appearing for the petitioner, submitted that the Courts below failed to consider the interpolation in the alleged rokka pattan, the very basis of the plaintiffs' claim which was admitted by PW 5, Mohini Mohan Dey and non consideration of the said apparent factual aspect and the evidence of PW 5 resulted in an error occasioning failure of justice in decreeing the suit. He further submitted that the suit land belonged to Zaminder Maharaja Sitangshu Kumar Acharjee Chowdhury as khash land. After the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act came into force the suit land, being chandina land, vested in the Government as khash land. Accordingly, record of right was correctly prepared in the name of the Government. Therefore, by the alleged pattan the plaintiffs' predecessor did not acquire any title to the suit land, both the Courts below committed error of law resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice in decreeing the suit and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. 

 7. Mr Sikder Mahmudur Raji, the learned Advocate appearing with Mr Md Bakiruddin Bhuiyan for the plaintiff-opposite-parties, on the other hand, submitted that the predecessor of the plaintiffs took rokka pattan of the suit land on 18th Kartic, 1351 BS from Maharaja Sitangshu Kumar Acharjee Chowdhury and since then had been possessing peacefully without any interference from any quarter. Accordingly, they acquired valid right, title and interest in the suit land, but the suit land was wrongly recorded as khash land in the record of right in the name of the Government which they came to know on 2-5-2002 and, as such, they instituted the suit for declaration of their title, the court below rightly decreed the suit. He further submitted that both the courts below having concurrently believed plaintiffs' case of settlement by rokka from its original owner and thus title in the suit land there is no scope of interference with the impugned judgment and decree by this Court in exercising revisional jurisdiction and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 12. Both the courts below concurrently found that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land for a long continuous period. But the question is, whether they are in possession for more than 60 years, because in order to acquire title by way of adverse possession the plaintiffs must prove their possession for more then 60 years as provided in Article 149 of the Limitation Act, 1908. The rokka pattan by which the plaintiffs' predecessor claimed to have taken pattan though not proved even if taken into consideration for the purpose of possession it appeared that the same is dated 18th Kartic 1351 BS corresponding to 2/3 November, 1944 and the suit was instituted on 2-1-2005, that is, before 60 years. Therefore, the plaintiffs did not acquire any title to the suit land by virtue of their possession.
